title: Private proxy double-encoding causes tool-call payload parse failures
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Several private deployment customers (notably an enterprise finance customer and a healthcare pilot) reported intermittent failures when invoking tool/function calls with structured JSON output. Failures present as either (a) our parser returning a 400 with `structured_parse_error` or (b) truncated responses where downstream tool invocations receive a single JSON string payload instead of an object. This only occurs for Private (VPC/on-prem) installs and reproducibly occurs when the customer traffic traverses an enterprise proxy/WAF that performs payload inspection and rewriting.

Environments affected:
- Redwood Private (VPC) behind customer-managed perimeter proxy (CrowdStrike/F5/BlueCoat-like appliances)
- Not observed in Hosted or Dedicated (cloud-managed) tenants

Customer reports and support tickets:
- CS-1172 (FinanceCorp): recurring failures in the morning batch job; reported tool-call JSON was received as a quoted/URL-encoded string by the service and parsing failed.
- CS-1189 (HealthPilot): streaming tool-call output intermittently truncated; customer saw JSON payload wrapped in an extra layer of quotes and escape sequences.
- Both escalations marked P0 due to production impact on customer workflows.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Use the standard tool-call request body with a nested JSON result (example below):
   {
     "tool_call": {
       "name": "lookup_account",
       "arguments": {"account_ids": ["acct_12345"], "metadata": {"source": "crm"}}
     }
   }
2) Send the POST to a Private deployment, but route the request through a proxy appliance configured to perform HTTP inspection + URL-encoding of suspicious payloads (config: inspect-json=true; urlencode-body=true).
3) Observe the server-side receive buffer: instead of a JSON object, the runtime receives a string: "{\"tool_call\":{\"name\":\"lookup_account\",\"arguments\":\"%7B%5C"account_ids%5C":%5B%5C"acct_12345%5C"%5D%7D\"}}"
4) Our parser treats that as a primitive string => structured parsing fails or downstream code thinks the tool returned a string.

Initial triage and root cause analysis:
- The customer proxies are not strictly 'corrupting' bytes, but they perform an inspection pass that can re-encode JSON payloads as URL-encoded strings (for DLP/inspection reasons) or wrap them in additional quotes when streamed chunk-by-chunk.
- Our streaming/structured-output parser expects either: (a) raw JSON frames for each tool-call structured output OR (b) a streaming sequence with explicit boundary markers. We did not anticipate the case where the body is still valid JSON but the inner structured field is a JSON-encoded string (double-encoded).
- The problem is most visible on Private installs because the customer's proxy sits between the client and the Redwood agent; Hosted/Dedicated requests do not cross those appliances.
- Some older language-model clients (used by customers) send tool-call arguments with application/x-www-form-urlencoded style or percent-encoded content; combined with the proxy behavior this results in nested encoding.

Technical trade-offs considered:
- Aggressively auto-decoding any string that 'looks like' JSON: good developer experience for customers but increases risk of decoding maliciously crafted inputs (potential injection) and could mask real client bugs.
- Require customers to set a header to opt into 'proxy-decoding' behavior: safer but requires customer coordination and slow support turnaround for high-severity incidents.

Proposed fix (short-term):
1) Parser hardening: implement a safe heuristic in the structured-output parser: when a field expected to be an object/array is a JSON string, attempt to safely unescape/decode once if and only if the decoded length is <= 1MB and the decoded payload begins with '{' or '['. Limit to 1 decode pass to avoid exponential decoding abuses.
2) Streaming decoder: when streaming chunk boundaries produce partial JSON that ends up quoted, attempt to assemble and decode the quoted payload across chunks (preserve backpressure semantics).
3) Add explicit telemetry/error codes for "double_encoded_payload" so we can measure prevalence and automatically open support tickets for affected customers.
4) Customer guidance: provide a KB entry and quick config snippet customers can add to their proxies to disable aggressive body re-encoding for Redwood endpoints (suggest using a header like X-Redwood-Allow-Raw: true).

Long-term fix / follow-ups:
- Add an agent-side proxy bypass header negotiation in Private deployments (agent communicates with customer proxy admin to get a minimal set of headers to avoid rewriting).
- Add unit + integration tests that simulate common enterprise proxy rewrites (URL-encoding, quote-wrapping, chunk reassembly) and run them in CI for the runtime package.
- Update SDK docs to recommend content-type and header knobs for on-prem customers using corporate proxies.

Implementation plan and rollout:
- Phase 1 (hotfix branch): implement the safe heuristic decoder and streaming reassembly. Add feature flag `parser.safe_double_decode=true` default ON for Private installs only. Target PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3482. (ETA: 3 days).
- Phase 2 (monitoring + rollout): deploy hotfix to internal staging and to one affected customer's non-prod environment for verification. Add telemetry to track `decoder.double_decode_count` and `decoder.decode_failure_count`. (ETA: 2 days).
- Phase 3 (customer rollouts and docs): ship KB article, provide per-customer remediation steps, and offer to coordinate proxy rule changes for high-impact customers. (ETA: 5 days).

Safety considerations and mitigations:
- Limit decoding attempts to a single pass and a small size limit to reduce risk from crafted payloads that try to force repeated decoding layers (DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH).
- Validate decoded JSON against expected schema for tool-call outputs - mismatched shapes should be rejected rather than blindly executed.
- Ensure telemetry does not include PII from customer payloads; only emit anonymized shape/size metrics and whether decoding was performed/failed.

Links / artifacts:
- PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3482 (draft)
- Support tickets: CS-1172, CS-1189
- Repro harness: internal repo: gitlab.redwood/simulate-proxies/proxy-harness (branch: encode-wrapping)
- Playbook for CS/SEs: docs/redwood/private/proxy-rewrites.md (internal)

Acceptance criteria:
- Parser successfully decodes single-level double-encoded tool-call payloads in Private test rig without false positives on Hosted/Dedicated tests.
- Telemetry reports decoding attempts and success rates.
- Customers confirm resolution (CS ack) and no longer see structured_parse_error for these cases.

Postmortem follow-ups (after incident close):
- Update onboarding doc for Private customers to include proxy config checklist.
- Add an integration test matrix covering common WAF vendors and default rewrite behaviors.
- Evaluate whether an agent-side Negotiation protocol (tiny header exchange) should be added to avoid future re-encodings.
